successors.name: Asuka Japan
successors.text: the Yamato realm that the Asuka period takes over: Cliopatria's Asuka Japan outline, from Kyushu to Fukushima

ledger.x: c. 250: the Yamato Kingship begins in the Nara Basin. 'The Yamato Kingship is usually believed to have begun c. 250'; the Yamato polity page gives mid-3rd to early 4th century depending on the researcher, with burial-mound evidence pointing to the later 3rd century.
Mid-5th century: the court's centre moves to the Kawachi Plain (Kondayama, Daisen tombs).
5th century: the tomb horizon reaches the whole later Asuka outline.
ledger.cp: Regional leaders of the east and south

ledger.x: 528: northern Kyushu passes to direct rule (Daizaifu).
After 527: the western lands under direct control.
After 527: the east and south under the miyake.
ledger.cp: Regional leaders of the east and south

ledger.x: 528: the realm reaches the Asuka outline.

wars.name: Yamato campaigns in Korea
wars.outcome: No land change recorded in the archipelago: Japanese troops allied with Baekje invaded Korea and fought Silla and Goguryeo; the page records no Yamato holding there.

wars.name: Iwai Rebellion
wars.outcome: Yamato victory: Iwai was overthrown and executed in 528 and the Daizaifu fortress ended Tsukushi's autonomy.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the pages give provinces, tomb horizons and a rebellion, no boundary.
